 Modhaus Turns K-Pop Fan Participation Into a Global Business With COSMO
 by 
 Zee Cindy 
 post_date_format( $post ) ); ?> 
 --> 
 November 6, 2026 
 in 
 Press Release 
 0 
 What if K-pop fans could do more than support their favorite artists? What if they could help decide which members perform together, choose title tracks, and shape a group’s creative direction? South Korean entertainment technology company Modhaus is turning that idea into a global business through COSMO , a fan participation platform that connects digital photocard collecting, blockchain-powered voting, and artist management. 
 With approximately 660,000 cumulative users, 22 million digital photocards issued, and KRW 26 billion in cumulative platform transaction volume , Modhaus has established a business model extending well beyond South Korea. Approximately 80% of its platform revenue comes from overseas , reflecting the international reach of its approach to K-pop fandom.
 Founded in November 2021 by CEO Jaden Jeong and co-founder Joseph Baek , Modhaus manages three K-pop groups, tripleS, ARTMS, and idntt , while developing an entertainment ecosystem in which fan participation and artist intellectual property (IP) reinforce each other.
 COSMO Gives Global K-Pop Fans a Voice in Artist Decisions
 Modhaus calls its approach Open Architecture Entertainment , a model that allows fans to participate directly in decisions traditionally controlled by entertainment agencies.
 The concept emerged from Jeong’s more than 25 years of experience in K-pop artist planning and production . Having worked with artists including Wonder Girls, 2PM, INFINITE, and Lovelyz, and having planned LOONA , he recognized the importance of building sustainable fandoms rather than relying exclusively on album success.
 His vision was to create groups whose members could be arranged in different combinations , much like LEGO blocks, with fans helping determine those combinations. That vision became reality with tripleS , a 24-member girl group designed around flexible unit formations and fan voting .
 In September 2022, Modhaus held its first fan vote, recording 10,800 votes to organize eight members into two units. By 2025, a unit selection vote had attracted 2.55 million votes , illustrating the growing scale of fan participation.
 At the center of this experience is COSMO: the Gate , an application where fans purchase and collect digital photocards called Objekts . These collectibles come with voting rights known as COMO , which fans use in voting events called Gravity .
 The votes influence actual artist activities, including unit formations and title track selections. Results are recorded on the blockchain, creating a transparent and tamper-resistant voting record.
 COSMO also enables fans to exchange Objekts , access artist content, and communicate through messaging, livestreaming, and community features. Despite its Web3 infrastructure, the application is designed for everyday K-pop fans. Users can sign in with email, digital wallets are created automatically, and Modhaus covers blockchain transaction fees.
 “We want voting to be more than simply holding a vote. We want it to be a process through which fans help shape the group’s identity together,”
 said Jaden Jeong.
 CEO Jaden Jeong. | Modhaus 
 From Digital Photocards to a Growing Entertainment Business
 Modhaus combines two complementary revenue streams : its COSMO platform and entertainment operations .
 The platform generates revenue through individual Objekt purchases and subscription products, while its entertainment business includes albums, digital music, concerts, VIP experiences, merchandise, advertising, and artist appearances. 
 This structure creates multiple ways to generate revenue from fan engagement while supporting artists’ activities. Objekt also provides artists with an additional income source, with photocard earnings settled through smart contracts after promotional periods conclude.
 “Through Objekt, Modhaus has created a business model that does not fail,”
 said Jeong, highlighting the company’s ambition to build a more sustainable entertainment business beyond traditional album sales.
 The company’s artist achievements demonstrate the commercial reach of its entertainment business.
 tripleS increased its first-week album sales from approximately 18,000 copies to 516,000 copies , representing nearly 30-fold growth . The group also won Best New Female Artist at the 2023 MAMA Awards and the 1theK Global Icon Award at the 2024 Melon Music Awards. 
 Meanwhile, ARTMS generated approximately USD 2.4 million in ticket revenue through a world tour spanning 18 cities in North America and Europe.
 Boy group idntt , which debuted in August 2025, ranked ninth in all-time first-week album sales among K-pop boy group debut releases and subsequently secured a win on KBS Music Bank.
 Together, Modhaus’s three groups sold more than one million albums in 2025 .
 Source: Modhaus 
 The company’s financial performance has also expanded. Revenue increased from KRW 20.4 billion in 2024 to KRW 32.3 billion in 2025 , with another KRW 16.6 billion recorded in the first half of 2026.
 Modhaus has now secured KRW 42.6 billion in total investment , including KRW 10 billion raised from Atinum Investment in July 2026, providing additional financial resources for its business development and international expansion.
 Expanding K-Pop’s Global Reach Through Tours and IP Partnerships
 With approximately 80% of COSMO’s platform revenue coming from overseas , Modhaus is building on its international fan base to expand its global entertainment business through concert tours, localized fan experiences, and strategic IP partnerships. 
 The company’s artists are bringing their music and performances to audiences across major international markets. ARTMS is touring North America in October 2026, with a European tour planned for January 2027.
 Meanwhile, tripleS is performing across Taiwan, Macau, and Japan in October, followed by a six-city North American tour scheduled for November. In Japan, Modhaus is also preparing for the group’s full-length album release, targeted for January 2027.
 Beyond live performances, Modhaus is creating new opportunities for international partners to engage K-pop audiences through its artist IP and COSMO platform. The company has secured overseas IP licensing and management agreements and is developing localized applications powered by COSMO’s existing infrastructure . It plans to begin operating external artist IP businesses in early 2027, expanding the commercial applications of its fan participation technology.
 Modhaus also strengthened its international business network through the 2026 Tourism Global Challenge , participating in a Shanghai roadshow where it introduced its business to local investors and potential partners. The program opened discussions with companies experienced in Chinese-speaking markets, exploring collaboration opportunities in IP merchandise, pop-up stores, Xiaohongshu and WeChat marketing, and livestream commerce .
 These initiatives extend Modhaus’s fan engagement model beyond digital interactions, creating opportunities for international audiences to connect with K-pop artists through concerts, fan events, exclusive merchandise, and immersive pop-up experiences. They also open new possibilities for partnerships across entertainment, retail, and cultural tourism.
 And today, Modhaus is actively seeking IP licensing, merchandise, and marketing partners in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Southeast Asia . In Japan, it aims to collaborate with music distribution companies, concert promoters, and fan event organizers, while its North American and European expansion focuses on concert promotion and premium fan experiences.
 By combining three established artist IPs, a global COSMO community of approximately 660,000 cumulative users, and adaptable platform infrastructure , Modhaus offers international partners a foundation for developing localized entertainment services, reaching engaged K-pop audiences, and creating new commercial opportunities around fan participation.
 Source: Modhaus 
 Building the Next Generation of Fan-Driven Entertainment
 Modhaus is advancing its Open Architecture Entertainment model with ambitious plans for new artists, international expansion, and a more immersive COSMO experience.
 The company plans to complete idntt’s 24-member lineup through fan voting , introduce a new global girl group , and expand COSMO’s interactive features to encourage deeper engagement.
 It is also experimenting with new ways to make live performances more accessible, beginning with a pay-what-you-want pricing pilot at Haseul’s solo concert in November 2026 .
 Building on its international fan base and growing artist portfolio, Modhaus aims to bring its fan-driven entertainment model to more markets through localized services, IP licensing, and strategic partnerships . By giving audiences a meaningful role in shaping the artists they love, the company is creating fresh opportunities for global K-pop experiences and commercial collaboration.
 Modhaus is participating in the 2026 TOURISM GLOBAL CHALLENGE program, an initiative led by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea and the Korea Tourism Organization to support promising Korean tourism companies seeking to expand into global markets.
